requirement_summary: Use the exact approved working title and show supervisor-pending status.
Model only the access-authorization layer and abstract outputs.
Represent LF and HF as logical reader-source labels.
Represent floors 1–16 with exactly 16 logical outputs.
Require no reader, controller, elevator hardware, device I/O, or network.
Complete required MVP before optional work.
notes: Optional work cannot gate required tests.

requirement_summary: Gate physical integration and commercial equivalence on supervisor approval.
Receive one complete credential frame per request.
Receive and retain one LF or HF source label.
Accept exactly 26 bits in the MVP.
Reject non-binary frame values.
Validate leading and trailing parity.
Extract facility and credential numbers.
Look up the composite credential key.
notes: Tuple key is not arithmetic addition.

requirement_summary: Deny unknown and disabled credentials with distinct reasons.
Receive one floor and validate range 1–16.
Grant only when the mapped permission bit is set.
Activate only the granted floor output.
Reject new requests as controller_busy while an output is active.
Deactivate the active output at configured expiry.
Failure creates no new activation and preserves only an existing authorized activation.
Return to idle and accept a valid request after timeout or reset.
notes: Covers timeout, manual reset, watchdog reset.

requirement_summary: Optionally support separately named additional Wiegand profiles.
Optionally support administrative or time-based authorization extensions.
Use the frozen PROJECT_WIEGAND_26 field allocation.
Use even leading and odd trailing parity regions.
Store source label separately and never infer it from frame bits.
notes: Identical frame may be LF or HF.

requirement_summary: Validate the required credential-record fields and ranges.
Use a composite key and reject duplicates.
Map floor 1 to bit 0 and floor 16 to bit 15; reject invalid masks.
Represent exactly 16 Boolean output channels.
Default output duration to 3000 ms and allow 100–30000 ms.
Use injectable monotonic simulated time.
Default watchdog timeout to 2000 ms.
Log every required grant, denial, error, timeout, and reset event.
Include all minimum event-schema fields when applicable.
Use monotonic sequence numbers and simulated timestamps.
Start and manually reset to all-inactive idle state.
Manual reset cancels timeout and logs once.
Invalid input cannot corrupt later processing.
Watchdog fault causes all-inactive reset, log, idle, and recovery.
Produce deterministic logical results for identical controlled runs.
notes: Host timing metrics excluded from equality.

requirement_summary: Use separately testable software responsibilities.
Perform no network access and require no hardware in normal execution.
Support Python 3.11+ with standard library plus pytest preferred.
Run all required automated tests through one documented pytest command.
Regenerate test data from a recorded seed or configuration ID.
Export machine-readable CSV or JSON results.
verification_method: Schema validation and parse round trip

requirement_summary: Use UTF-8 project text/data and repository-relative internal paths.
Handle invalid input/configuration with deterministic errors and continued operation.
notes: Programmer defects need not be masked.

requirement_summary: Optionally add persistent local credential storage.
Optionally add a GUI or enhanced CLI.
Consider physical adapters only after a separately approved scope change.
Trace every required requirement to planned verification.
Cover required frame, credential, authorization, floor, and busy cases.
Cover output timing, resets, watchdog, recovery, and log completeness.
Test both source labels and deterministic replay.
Run scalability experiments at 10, 100, 1000, and 10000 credentials.
Collect all frozen counts, timing statistics, throughput, size, and seed/config ID.
Preserve controlled inputs, expected results, actual results, and evaluation.
Record environment and limits for timing or throughput results.
Optionally evaluate extra sizes or profiles after required experiments.
Label all frozen behavior and values as proposed project decisions.
Prohibit unsupported commercial technology and electrical claims.
Exclude physical elevator, safety, mains, certification, and installation behavior.
Limit performance and recovery conclusions to the Python model and test environment.
